standard_prerequisites.name: Canonical Liouville form on the cotangent bundle
standard_prerequisites.statement: lambda_std is the standard Liouville one-form on T*Sigma, with d lambda_std the canonical symplectic form.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the target form whose pull-back is computed at source lines 754-761 and 802.

standard_prerequisites.name: Collar coordinates and the normalised primitive
standard_prerequisites.statement: On the collar A_C = [0,rho) x S^1 the primitive nu_0 has the displayed form with a constant a_C.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is used to write f_0 explicitly at source lines 765-772.

standard_prerequisites.name: Moser's trick
standard_prerequisites.statement: Given a family of forms mu_t with mu_0 = mu_1 up to exactness one solves X_t interior dmu_t = -(d/dt)mu_t and integrates to an isotopy pulling mu_1 back to mu_0 up to an exact form.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the whole second half of the proof, source lines 777-808.

core_obligations: Work first in the collar A = A_C: on a small neighbourhood W of the diagonal in A x A define the explicit map kappa_0(r,s,R,S) = (R, s, R(S-s), (r^2-R^2)/2) and check that it restricts to a diffeomorphism on the interior and sends the diagonal to the zero section (source lines 741-752).

Verify kappa_0^* lambda_std = -nu_1 + nu_2 + d f_0 with f_0(r,s,R,S) = (a_C - R^2/2)(s-S), and check the two boundary identities f_0(0,s,0,S) = -integral over [z_1,z_2] of nu_0 and d f_0(0,s,0,S) = nu_1 - nu_2 (source lines 753-773).

Extend from the collar to all of Sigma x Sigma: choose f_1 : U -> R agreeing with f_0 near the boundary part and with f_1 identically zero on the diagonal and d f_1 = nu_1 - nu_2 there, and a map kappa_1 agreeing with kappa_0 near that boundary part, a diffeomorphism on the interior, with kappa_1(Delta) = 0_Sigma (source lines 775-776).

Apply Moser's trick with mu_t := t kappa_1^*(lambda_std) + (1-t)(nu_2 - nu_1): the two forms define the same orientation so d mu_t is symplectic away from the boundary, and one chooses X_t solving X_t interior d mu_t + kappa_1^* lambda_std - nu_2 + nu_1 - d f_1 = 0, which vanishes on the diagonal and near the boundary part (source lines 777-793).

Integrate X_t to an isotopy phi_t coinciding with kappa_0 near U cap (boundary x boundary), compute that (d/dt) phi_t^* mu_t = phi_t^* d(mu_t(X_t) + f_1), and conclude phi_1^* kappa_1^* lambda_std = -nu_1 + nu_2 + d f with f given by the displayed integral, so that psi := kappa_1 o phi_1 has all the required properties (source lines 794-808).

proof_roadmap.step: Explicit collar model kappa_0 and verification of the pull-back and boundary identities.
Extension f_1, kappa_1 from the collar to the whole neighbourhood.
Moser's trick: the family mu_t, the orientation remark and the vector field equation.
Integration, the exactness computation and the definition of psi.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `l:Weinstein` at source lines 715-738: there are neighbourhoods U of the diagonal in Sigma x Sigma and V of the zero section in T*Sigma together with a map psi restricting to a diffeomorphism on the interior, sending the diagonal to the zero section and pulling lambda_std back to nu_2 - nu_1 + d f, with f explicitly normalised on the boundary; in collar coordinates psi has the displayed explicit form. The author's proof (source lines 740-809) is a full two-stage construction: it first writes down the explicit collar model kappa_0 and verifies both the pull-back identity and the two boundary identities for f_0, which is where the constant a_C and the normalised primitive are consumed (lines 741-773); it then extends that model to a neighbourhood of the whole diagonal by choosing f_1 and kappa_1 with prescribed behaviour near the boundary part (lines 775-776), and finishes with a textbook application of Moser's trick in which the orientation comparison lets one solve for X_t, the vanishing properties of X_t are checked, and the exactness computation produces f as an integral of mu_t(X_t) + f_1 along the isotopy (lines 777-808). The statement contains the conclusion and the explicit formula but none of the construction, and the explicit formula is itself part of the statement rather than a hypothesis.
